Beállítom A New York-i székhelyű Bizottság az Újságírók Védelméért (CPJ) nevű szervezet bejelentette , hogy Panyi Szabolcs magyar újságírót is kitünteti a november 19-én New Yorkban megrendezendő Nemzetközi Sajtószabadság-díj átadóján. Panyi Szabolcs jelenleg a VSquare újságírója, korábban Direkt36 oknyomozó portálnál dolgozott. Idén ő tárta fel Szijjártó Péter bizalmas kapcsolatát Szergej Lavrov orosz külügyminiszterrel. Panyi a választási kampányban a kormánypropaganda, majd a hatóságok támadásainak célkeresztjébe került. „Az idei díjazottak példázzák az újságírók elszántságát és bátorságát világszerte […] Csupán azért, mert híreket közöltek, célponttá váltak, bebörtönözték, száműzték és megfigyelés alá vonták őket. Megtiszteltetés számunkra, hogy elismerhetjük az igazság feltárása iránti elkötelezettségüket” – mondta a szervezet közleménye szerint Jodie Ginsberg, a CPJ vezérigazgatója. A közleményben Panyi Szabolcsról azt írják: Panyi Szabolcs Európa egyik vezető oknyomozó újságírója. Az egykori Orbán-rezsim működését feltáró riportjai nem csupán Magyarországon gyakoroltak hatalmas hatást, hanem az európai politikai vitát is befolyásolták. Az újságíró nemzetbiztonsági forrásokhoz is hozzáfért, és az orosz befolyásszerző műveletekről szóló riportjai miatt kémkedéssel vádolták meg . Panyi Szabolcs nemzetbiztonságról, külföldi befolyásról, korrupcióról és politikai hatalmi viszonyokról szóló riportjai döntő szerepet játszottak az orosz befolyási hálózatok leleplezésében Magyarországon, valamint a választások előtti közvélemény formálásában, ami végül az Orbán-kormány vereségéhez vezetett – írják. Panyi Szabolcs a Facebook-oldalán azt írta: „Ezt az elismerést azoknak a bátor kollégáknak, forrásoknak és olvasóknak ajánlom, akik életben tartották a független újságírást Magyarországon – és akik nap mint nap emlékeztetnek rá, hogy a hatalom visszaéléseinek feltárása mindig megéri a kockázatot. Sokat elárul az elmúlt tizenhat év magyarországi viszonyairól, hogy ez az első alkalom, hogy az 1991 óta átadott díjat egy EU-tagállam újságírója kapja meg. Az Orbán-rezsimnek azonban vége, mi viszont még mindig itt vagyunk.” Panyi mellett egy kolumbiai, egy eritreai, egy salvadori, egy libanoni és egy mianmari újságírót tüntet ki idén a CPJ. Az amerikai szervezet többször felszólalt a Telex újságíróit ért inzultusok miatt is, például akkor amikor Csákberény polgármestere, Vécsei László fizikai erőszakot alkalmazva lökte ki két kolléganőnket egy Semjén Zsolt miniszterelnök-helyettes részvételével zajló sajtótájékoztatóról, vagy amikor Fóton rendőrök vitték el kollégáinkat , akik azért várakoztak, hogy kérdezzenek Orbán Viktortól. Search the Public Notice Portal A FORMER Argos store in Worcester city centre could become a bank. Plans for the empty shop in The Shambles have been put forward by Delikatesy Smaczek, which runs several Polish delicatessens across the UK. The company intends to let the unit to Barclays, the Local Democracy Reporting Service understands. The store has been vacant since 2021 despite Lindum Leisure Limited being given permission to turn it into a Carousel Bar in March 2023. That planning permission has now expired and a fresh scheme has been submitted to Worcester City Council by a different applicant. SCHEME: Plans by Delikatesy Smaczek to turn the former Argos store into a bank (Image: Roberts Librick) Delikatesy Smaczek says in its plans: “The proposals embrace the opportunity to transform a currently underutilised, vacant building within a prime city centre location into a positive contribution for the local economy. “It is proposed that the existing retail unit known as 1-2 The Shambles will be refurbished to provide a bank facility. “The building will remain the same size, no extension or demolitions are proposed except when modifying internal areas and altering parts of the building envelope to suit new use of the building. “Internally, certain areas will be rationalised and made into larger, more flexible spaces. “Externally, new energy-efficient cladding will improve its appearance, whilst all doors and windows will be replaced.” Proposed works would include the installation of an ATM and roof repairs to the building, which has become a target for graffiti after sitting empty for five years. “An active frontage will be retained across the front and side elevations at ground floor,” the plans state. Read more M&S Foodhall gets permission to move to new home Fears live music venue could close if 'heartbreaking' flats plan given green light City centre parking spaces will be used for new SEND sixth form Empty County Hall still costing taxpayers £1m a year as NHS takeover calls grow “The ATM will further help to drive footfall to this part of the centre, providing significant benefits to the vitality and viability of the primary shopping frontage. “The proposed works will facilitate the occupation of a long-term vacant site in a prominent location and will facilitate the creation of an active town centre use. “Not only will this be beneficial in terms of local employment levels, and the health of the city centre, but it will provide significant improvements to the appearance of the building and therefore the wider streetscene.” Earlier this year, council leader Lynn Denham said it was disappointing nothing had been done with the site years after planning approval was given. https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/news/sto.text: Here are the latest cases from the region's courts: PENKHULL: Thirty-four-year-old Prince Makuvasa has been hit with a £405 court bill after he spat inside a police vehicle. North Staffordshire Justice Centre heard police were called to Marchwood Court, in Penkhull , just after midnight on September 12. Prosecutor Helen Shipley said Makuvasa was taken into the back of a police car and while there he put his head down and started spitting. He was told not to spit and officers put a spit hood on him. The police car needed a professional clean which cost £190. Makuvasa, of Marchwood Court, Penkhull, pleaded guilty to criminal damage. Paige Morgan, mitigating, said Makuvasa was under the influence at the time. She said he had been choked in an earlier incident and he asked officers if he could spit in the car. Miss Morgan added: "He did not give the police chance to respond." Magistrates fined Makuvasa £93 and ordered him to pay £190 compensation, £85 costs, and a £37 surcharge. BURSLEM: Twenty-two-year-old Brandon Pennell, of Waterloo Road, Burslem , has admitted drink-driving, disqualified driving, and driving without insurance on September 7. North Staffordshire Justice Centre heard the offending happened about six weeks after he was sentenced to 15 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, and handed a nine-month driving ban at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court for burglary and taking a vehicle without the owner's consent. Magistrates sent the case to the crown court and Pennell will appear there on a date to be fixed administratively. His bail was extended. NORTH STAFFORDSHIRE: Thirty-nine-year-old Renatas Butavicius, of HMP Maidstone, is charged with possession of a class B drug with intent to supply and possession of a weapon capable of discharging a noxious substance. He will reappear at North Staffordshire Justice Centre with a Lithuanian interpreter on Tuesday, October 13 and he remains in custody. WATERHOUSES: Thirty-six-year-old Robert Preston, of Portland Place, Waterhouses , has admitted two charges of assault occasioning actual bodily harm. His sentence hearing has been adjourned and he will next appear at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court for a mention hearing on November 2. His bail was extended. HANLEY: Twenty-eight-year-old Dominik Tancos, of Poundlock Avenue, Hanley , has appeared at North Staffordshire Justice Centre charged with two offences of theft from Hanley Boots. His case has been adjourned and he will next appear at the same court on Thursday, October 15. His bail was extended. Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search

https://www.witn.com/2026/10/13/warsaw-c.text: Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google Warsaw commissioners voted no confidence in Mayor Wesley Boykin and Commissioner Ebony Wills-Wells during a town meeting Monday night. The vote was 4-1, with Wills-Wells as the lone no vote. Wills-Wells says she then made a request to rescind her no vote because of conflict of interest because she says she recognized the situation involved her. The no-confidence vote comes as Boykin and Wills-Wells came into possession of a document that contains personal information of town employees that they are not permitted to have access to. Despite the no-confidence vote, the resolution does not remove Boykin and Wills-Wells from their positions. Commissioner Cheryl Smith read the resolution Monday night. “Mayor Boykin and Commissioner Wills-Wells were in possession of a document for three weeks before disclosing to the board and the town manager the existence of the said document at the July 2026 board meeting, and whereas it has been three months Mayor Boykin and Commissioner Wills-Wells disclosed to the town board the existence of the document, and they still refuse to provide a copy of the document to the town manager or the town attorney.” The document contained personal information about town employees, including Social Security numbers, the resolution said. Wills-Wells says an employee brought the document to her but that she does not know who gave the document to the employee. “I do not know where it came from,” she said. “I just know that a town employee brought it to me in confidence and they entrusted that the matter would be addressed properly.” Commissioner Jack Hawes said a meeting was scheduled last week with Boykin and Town Manager Lea Turner to discuss the document. “The town attorney, the town manager, and the mayor had a meeting in which the mayor was supposed to turn over those documents, and he still refused,” Hawes said. Hawes says that is when commissioners decided to craft the resolution. “We felt like he had ample opportunity, and Miss Wells had ample opportunity to turn those documents in,” Hawes said. “You’re going on four months now, and the town attorney scheduled a meeting between those three to actually discuss that, and he still refused to turn them in.” Wills-Wells told WITN the document had been destroyed and denied sending it to anyone. “I don’t have the document; the document has been destroyed,” she said. “That has been a question that has been asked as well, and no, the document was not sent to anyone by me, as those false allegations and defamation to my character were given and made by individuals on this board as well as leadership.” She said she believes she and Boykin are being treated unfairly because they stand up for what is right. Wills-Wells also claimed she destroyed the document after an email from the interim town attorney, which she characterized as asking her to do something illegal. “There was an email that was sent out asking for me to do something illegal from the interim town attorney; it came directly from the interim town attorney, and I responded to that email in regards to the concerns and just the baffling of the ask of me and the document was destroyed,” she said. Boykin declined WITN’s interview request. In a statement to WITN, he did not address the document. He said: “I am a native son of Warsaw. The residents of this town deserves leaders with a vision for a better day, and all leaders should commit to that vision as I have. We must commit to the Common Core Values that I presented in June, but voted down by a 4-1 majority last night. These same individuals voted down a commitment to the NCLM Civility Program. I cannot deflect my commitment to improving services to Warsaw residents, by focusing on individuals who publicly rejected a commitment to civility and adopting core values and performance goals. Any measure of leadership confidence that matters most, rests in the hands of the Warsaw voters.” clarification: A previous version of this story stated that Willis-Wells did not know who gave the document to her. It's been clarified to say she did not know who gave the document to the employee who in turn brought it to her. Copyright 2026 WITN. All rights reserved. https://www.countypress.co.uk/news/26644.text: Exclusive Court Isle Of Wight Man hit woman with glass at Isle of Wight pub after 'racist' comment Court Isle Of Wight Exclusive by Court reporter Share 0 Comments John Kattenhorn appeared at the Isle of Wight Crown Court (Image: IWCP) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A pub glass attack after a row over a 'racist' comment has ended in a suspended prison sentence for an Isle of Wight man. John Kattenhorn, 50, of no fixed address, appeared at the Isle of Wight Crown Court on Friday, October 16. He pleaded guilty to occasioning actual bodily harm and possession of cannabis on September 21, 2024. Prosecuting, Tim Devlin told the court the incident started when Kattenhorn made a comment about queuing up at a soup kitchen to another woman who was Polish at The Veteran pub in Ryde. The woman's friend threw the remains of her drink at him after telling him not to be racist. Read more Drunk man who repeatedly pinched woman's bottom at pub narrowly avoids prison Former lorry driver banned from the road for over two years for drink-driving Kattenhorn then hit the woman with his glass, which did not break but did cause injury, court heard. A scuffle broke out and another man at the pub was accidentally knocked over. Kattenhorn has 22 previous convictions from 41 offences. Defending, Juliet Osborne said Kattenhorn's offence was an 'abberation' after a long period of staying out of trouble and he was 'genuinely remorseful'. Sentencing, Judge William Ashworth said Kattenhorn had tried his best 'to get away with it' after pleading guilty on the day of his trial. He was handed a ten-month prison sentence, suspended for two years and ordered not to enter licensed premises for six months.
